newsitem.title: KYRGYZSTAN: Cen Asian states, NATO plan peacekeeping exercise.
newsitem.headline: Cen Asian states, NATO plan peacekeeping exercise.

text.p: Defence ministers from three former Soviet republics in Central Asia will meet a senior NATO official in Kyrgyzstan to hammer out details of a peacekeeping exercise, a Kyrgyz defence official said on Thursday.
Oleg Chechel, a senior Kyrgyz defence ministry official, told Reuters the ministers would meet General John Sheehan, Supreme Allied Commander Atlantic, in the capital Bishkek on Sunday.
"The joint exercises will take place over 10 days in the first half of September," Chechel said.
He said the exercises, taking place under NATO's "Partnership for Peace" programme, would be held near the Kazakh town of Chimkent and the Uzbek town of Chirchik.
The three republics provide troops for a CIS peacekeeping force in neighbouring Tajikistan, devastated by a four-year civil war.
The announcement came amid a storm of angry words from the Kremlin, which is fiercely opposed to any eastward expansion of NATO.

The Kremlin on Wednesday accused NATO and its Secretary-General Javier Solana, who is currently touring some of the former Soviet republics, of pursuing a covert anti-Moscow policy. NATO denied the charge.
Dependent on Moscow for aid and on Russian pipelines for the export of their energy wealth, none of the Kremlin's former colonies in Central Asia are pushing for NATO membership.
